newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock index futures end short week on upswing.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock index futures end short week on upswing.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures ended an abbreviated session sharply higher, with S&P 500s reaching yet another all-time high settlement at 927.75.

Bullish U.S. employment data triggered the rally. The Labor Department said the U.S. unemployment rate bounced back to 5.0 percent in June after falling to a near 24-year low of 4.8 percent in May. Many analysts had not expected a rise in the jobless rate.
Nonfarm payrolls grew by 217,000, slightly lower than expected. Average hourly earnings, a barometer of inflation, increased by four cents, the same rise as in May.

September S&P 500 futures shot up immediately on the news, climbing the opening 7.00 point limit and then adding to gains after a mandated two-minute trading halt. The contract set an all-time high of 929.00.

On top of the rise in unemployment and mild hourly earnings gain, an advance in September bond futures through the February high of 113-09 exacerbated the move in stock futures, said Jeff Feeney, analyst with Smith Barney Inc. in Chicago.
"As long as we continue to see solid earnings growth as well as a stable interest rate environment, stocks can continue to expand," Feeney said.

He predicted the 950.00 level in S&P 500 futures was surmountable in the medium term, but cautioned that the extent of the rise will hinge on second-quarter earnings that companies begin to release in the next couple of weeks.
"If you start to see disappointing earnings, that will really knock the legs out of this rally," Feeney said.
Floor traders in S&Ps said that after the initial runup, prices dipped at midmorning as local traders took profits and others also began to square up before the long holiday weekend.
Equity futures trading ended at 1215 CDT/1715 GMT.
One U.S. investment house was a particularly strong seller of S&P 500 futures through the morning, trading at least 2,500 contracts, floor traders said.
They described overall volume on the session as moderate, including a burst of buying on the close involving a handful of big houses that sent the contract back up toward the session high.

September S&P 500s ended up 12.25 points at 927.75, Nasdaq 100s up 12.00 at 1001.25, Russell 2000s up 2.00 points at 401.50, Nikkei 225 index futures down 100.0 at 20,260.0 and Midcap 400s up 2.95 points at 297.30. ((Chicago Derivatives Desk: 312-408-8750)) email:derivatives@reuters.com
